issues: Covers rose by 5 (0.42%) week on week and spend per head rose by £0.04 (0.18%).
Sales rose by £510.30 (2%) week on week and were £2,596.52 (11.05%) above target.
Food and drinks variance was 3.8% (food 4.3%, wet 0.4%).
Google rating for the week was 5.00, against a target of 40 five star reviews a week.
The site is still looking to hire a sushi chef, and who will lead that hire is to be confirmed; Gerry is training as part time sushi cover and the head chef will train a sushi chef this week.
A two week Deliveroo 30% off promotion starts on Monday 12/10, with Shoreditch in the first wave; whether to run a Halloween event is still open.
FOH standards are inconsistent across different managers.
BOH punctuality must follow the handbook, and at closing 10 to 15 minutes are allowed for admin, with compliance done first before cleaning starts.
On Thursday, with only one table in, a ramen was served directly from the pass and the guest complained it was lukewarm and said they would not come back.
Desserts can be made before 10pm, and last orders for hot food and sushi were at 9:30pm.

Kitchen points: no takeaway boxes for staff, Aashish to be trained on presentation of squid tempura and chicken katsu curry, extra items should print on the ramen section printer, and FOH should upsell edamame.
Rota changes: on Fridays one person goes home at 4pm and the next starts at 5pm, and staff choose only one day off.
The Monday to Wednesday staggered break rule set last week is still not being followed.
Gerry is to be updated, with Sophie, about changing the pot.
Shoreditch Town Hall was contacted about future catering and event opportunities through the B2B channel.
The delivery rating improved from 4.4 to 4.5.
FOH labour fell by about 2% because of longer breaks, while BOH labour rose with three to four chefs on.
Kaitlin Docherty found an unaddressed refund from 07/10, where a delivery customer received only one bag and the meal deal had spilled.
In the meeting Shoreditch was told to push for 45 five star Google reviews a week (the next steps still say 40).
A sushi chef candidate who trialled at Soho was good at rolling but needs fish cutting training, arranged for Thursday and Sunday; the new sushi chef is due to start next week.
Managers may collect staff phones at the start of each shift and keep them on the bar, and BOH lateness is to be tracked on Kobas with sit down meetings on attendance expectations.
After the lukewarm ramen complaint (from a former B2B customer), BOH must turn the heat up and make sure the broth is fully boiling before serving.
Staff from Shoreditch or Lakeside who want extra Saturday hours can be redirected to Soho.

Kei Cannon flagged that the AM dashboard showed wrong figures (very low labour efficiency) for Lakeside, Soho and Shoreditch; Kaitlin Docherty said the variance reports were filled in late on Sunday night and corrected on Monday morning, and the dashboard will reload overnight.

Region: Ziang Lin introduced a mandatory seating upsell at all sites from 13/10: staff place the drinks menu from the marketing stand in the middle of the table and immediately offer edamame, and kitchens boil a large batch of edamame in advance so it can be blanched for five seconds when ordered.
Region: Kaitlin Docherty will send daily delivery performance (red, amber, green) to the group chats every day between 10:30 and 12:00 from 14/10.

Weekly sales reached about £26,000, beating target by about £2,600 on stronger weekend evening trade, and a B2B push around Shoreditch Town Hall events lifted Saturday from £2,700 to £4,500 (AM Updates 14/10).
Wage revenue was 26.74% because of heavy discounting and training for Angel and head chef Jerry, who is training in sushi after Daryl left (AM Updates 14/10).
Food cost fell by 2% to 25.74% and SPH reached £21 after the back to basics push of drinks menus on tables and edamame offered on arrival (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: Soho and Shoreditch have a temporary 25% wage revenue target for the next six weeks while heavy promotions run; other sites keep their current targets (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: a level 8 Halloween ramen with a super spicy factory chilli paste is launching with a video; one bag per site, about a teaspoon per bowl (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: snooze out of stock items on both Deliverect and the POS, or the whole delivery order fails (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: wage revenue baseline is 21% with up to 2% leeway; drinks cost moves to management, food cost to head chefs, new OKRs due end of November (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: a temporary reserve stock buffer (about £300) was agreed for the English sites to stop stockouts (AM Updates 14/10).
